fullPassage: Human beings are endlessly innovative. Over the centuries, we have created many amazing ideas and inventions in order to solve some of the most difficult problems in history. However, the inspiration for many of these ideas and inventions came from nature. There is even a name for this field: biomimetics. Biomimetics takes advantage of the fact that nature has been undergoing a process of trial and error for billions of years. Over that time, it has perfected many systems and processes that allow plants and animals to survive in challenging circumstances and harsh environments. Therefore, throughout history, humans have been looking to nature for solutions to problems and ideas for inventions. The bodies of birds, for example, inspired the design of airplanes, while the water-resistant qualities of lotus flowers have been copied to make waterproof paint. Today, many new and exciting applications of biomimetics are being considered by scientists. For example, the strong silk used by spiders to make their webs may lead engineers to a flexible material that could be used to make bridge cables. Scientists have also been carefully studying animals that dive deep into the water to learn how they lower their brain temperatures and slow their metabolisms. It is hoped that this can help doctors find a way to treat seriously injured patients by putting their bodies into a similar state. Biomimetic research is also being done on a wide variety of other ideas. A strong illustration is research on how plant leaves could be used as the model for a new kind of solar panel. A substance mussels use to attach themselves to rocks is similarly being studied and copied in order to create a non-toxic glue for surgeons. Ultimately, biomimetics creates a new kind of relationship between humans and nature. Instead of treating animals, plants, and microbes as resources to be controlled or harvested, we are now looking at them as teachers with valuable information to share.

questions.passage: Human beings are endlessly innovative. Over the centuries, we have created many amazing ideas and inventions in order to solve some of the most difficult problems in history. However, the inspiration for many of these ideas and inventions came from nature. There is even a name for this field: biomimetics. Biomimetics takes advantage of the fact that nature has been undergoing a process of trial and error for billions of years. Over that time, it has perfected many systems and processes that allow plants and animals to survive in challenging circumstances and <u>harsh</u> environments. Therefore, throughout history, humans have been looking to nature for solutions to problems and ideas for inventions. The bodies of birds, for example, inspired the design of airplanes, while the water-resistant qualities of lotus flowers have been copied to make waterproof paint. Today, many new and exciting applications of biomimetics are being considered by scientists. For example, the strong silk used by spiders to make their webs may lead engineers to a flexible material that could be used to make bridge cables. Scientists have also been carefully studying animals that dive deep into the water to learn how they lower their brain temperatures and slow their metabolisms. It is hoped that this can help doctors find a way to treat seriously injured patients by putting their bodies into a similar state. Biomimetic research is also being done on a wide variety of other ideas. A strong illustration is research on how plant leaves could be used as the model for a new kind of solar panel. A substance mussels use to attach themselves to rocks is similarly being studied and copied in order to create a non-toxic glue for surgeons. Ultimately, biomimetics creates a new kind of relationship between humans and nature. Instead of treating animals, plants, and microbes as resources to be controlled or harvested, we are now looking at them as teachers with valuable information to share.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 harsh와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: harsh=혹독한 / mild=온화한 / gentle=부드러운 / warm=따뜻한 / severe=가혹한
det.analysis:
① mild: 온화한 — harsh의 반대예요

② gentle: 부드러운 — 반대에 가까워요

③ warm: 따뜻한 — 온도라 의미가 달라요

④ severe: 가혹한 — harsh(혹독한)의 동의어 ←정답
det.tip: harsh environments = 혹독한 환경 → severe.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 copied와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: copied=모방된 / created=창조된 / destroyed=파괴된 / imitated=모방된 / ignored=무시된
det.analysis:
① created: 창조된 — 새로 만드는 것이라 의미가 달라요

② destroyed: 파괴된 — 뜻이 반대예요

③ imitated: 모방된 — copied(모방된)의 동의어 ←정답

④ ignored: 무시된 — 관련이 없어요
det.tip: have been copied = 모방되었다 → imitated.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 difficult와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: difficult=어려운 / hard=어려운 / easy=쉬운 / serious=심각한 / common=흔한
det.analysis:
① hard: 어려운 — difficult의 동의어라 반의어가 아니에요

② easy: 쉬운 — difficult(어려운)의 반의어 ←정답

③ serious: 심각한 — 의미축이 달라요

④ common: 흔한 — 빈도라 의미가 달라요
det.tip: most difficult problems ↔ easy(쉬운).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 valuable와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: valuable=귀중한 / worthless=쓸모없는 / precious=소중한 / useful=유용한 / rare=드문
det.analysis:
① worthless: 쓸모없는 — valuable(귀중한)의 반의어 ←정답

② precious: 소중한 — valuable의 동의어예요

③ useful: 유용한 — valuable과 비슷한 뜻이에요

④ rare: 드문 — 희소성이라 의미축이 달라요
det.tip: valuable information ↔ worthless(쓸모없는).

questions.passage:
(A) After the accident, the injured man was in a very weak <u>state</u> for several weeks.

(B) France is a powerful <u>state</u> in Europe with a long and proud history.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 state의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: state: (A) 상태 (B) 국가
det.analysis:
① (A) 국가 (B) 상태: (A)는 몸의 '상태'라 반대로 짝지어졌어요

② (A) 진술 (B) 국가: (A)는 '상태'예요

③ (A) 상태 (B) 말하다: (B)는 유럽의 '국가'예요

④ (A) 상태 (B) 국가: 다친 사람의 몸 '상태' + 유럽의 강한 '국가' ←정답
det.tip: in a weak state = 상태 vs a powerful state = 국가.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a doctor who is specially trained to perform operations on people's bodies"

det.korean: patient=환자 / scientist=과학자 / surgeon=외과 의사 / engineer=기술자
det.analysis:
① patient: 환자 — 수술을 받는 사람이라 반대예요

② scientist: 과학자 — 수술을 하는 사람이 아니에요

③ surgeon: 외과 의사 — 몸에 수술을 하도록 훈련받은 의사 ←정답

④ engineer: 기술자 — 정의와 달라요
det.tip: trained to perform operations → 외과 의사(surgeon).

questions.passage: Biomimetics takes advantage of the fact that nature has been __________ (undergo) a process of trial and error for billions of years. Over that time, it has perfected many systems and processes that allow plants and animals to survive.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: undergo → undergoing: 'has been + __________'는 현재완료진행형이라 -ing 형태로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'nature has been __________'에서 'has been' 뒤에는 -ing가 와서 '~해 오고 있다'라는 현재완료진행을 나타내요. 자연이 수십억 년간 시행착오를 '겪어 오고 있다'는 뜻이라 undergo를 undergoing으로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 undergo를 undergoing으로 써요.
det.tip: has been + -ing = ~해 오고 있다 (현재완료진행).

questions.passage: Ultimately, biomimetics creates a new kind of relationship between humans and nature. Instead of __________ (treat) animals, plants, and microbes as resources to be controlled, we are now looking at them as teachers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: treat → treating: 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 써요.
det.analysis:
'Instead of __________'에서 of는 전치사라 뒤에 동명사가 와야 해요. '동물·식물·미생물을 자원으로 대하는 것 대신에'라는 뜻이라 treat를 동명사 treating으로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 treat를 treating으로 써요.
det.tip: instead of + 동명사(treating) = ~하는 것 대신에.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: trial and error=시행착오 / cause and effect=인과 / rest and peace=휴식과 평화 / loss and gain=손익
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤 'for billions of years(수십억 년 동안)'와 뒤 문장 '많은 체계를 완성해 왔다'가 단서예요.

① trial and error: 자연이 수십억 년간 '시행착오'를 거쳐 체계를 다듬었어요 ←정답

② cause and effect: 인과는 완성 과정과 안 맞아요

③ rest and peace: 휴식·평화는 문맥과 무관해요

④ loss and gain: 손익도 무관해요
det.tip: a process of ______ for billions of years → 시행착오(trial and error).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: enemies=적 / teachers=스승 / tools=도구 / strangers=낯선 이

빈칸 뒤 'with valuable information to share(나눌 귀중한 정보를 가진)'와 앞의 '통제·수확할 자원 대신'이 단서예요.

① enemies: 적은 배울 대상이 아니에요

② teachers: 귀중한 정보를 나눠 주는 '스승'으로 자연을 봐요 ←정답

③ tools: 도구는 오히려 자원처럼 쓰는 관점이라 반대예요

④ strangers: 낯선 이는 정보를 나눈다는 흐름과 안 맞아요
det.tip: looking at them as ______ with valuable information → 스승(teachers).
